paragraphs: Architectural and civil drafters (corresponding to O*NET 17-3011.00 Architectural and Civil Drafters on the US side) prepare detailed drawings of architectural and structural features of buildings, or drawings and topographical relief maps for civil engineering projects such as highways, bridges and public works, and apply knowledge of building materials, engineering practices and mathematics to complete drawings. Common job titles include Architectural Designer, Architectural Drafter, Architectural Draftsman, CAD Designer, CAD Tech, CADD Drafter, Civil Drafter, Drafting Technician, Draftsman and Draftsperson. Daily tasks include producing drawings with computer-aided drafting systems (CAD) or with plotters and hand tools; analysing the impact of building codes, local regulations and spatial and site requirements on the design; drawing rough and detailed scale plans of foundations, buildings and structures from preliminary concepts, sketches, engineering calculations and specification sheets; coordinating structural, electrical and mechanical designs and determining how building floor plans should be presented; explaining drawings to production or construction teams and adjusting them as needed; obtaining and assembling the data needed to complete building design and visiting construction sites to collect survey data; using CAD to lay out and plan interior room arrangements in commercial buildings; representing architects or engineers on construction sites under supervision to verify that construction matches the design and advising on corrections; reviewing sketches, drawings and specifications for conformity with the design concept; drawing maps, charts and profiles using cross-sections and survey data to show elevations, terrain contours, underground strata and structures; determining the work sequence and presentation method for orthographic or isometric drawings; completing and reproducing drawings and document sets by such methods as blueprints or photography to the required medium and reproduction specifications; conducting or supervising field surveys, inspections and technical investigations; training other technicians and drafters; correlating, interpreting and modifying topographic survey, well logging and geophysical exploration data; drafting plan and detail drawings for structural facilities such as highways, sewage systems and embankments; preparing cost estimates, contracts, tender documents and technical reports under the supervision of an architect or engineer; determining procedures and instructions to design specifications and required material quantities; determining the quality, cost, strength and quantity of materials needed and completing material lists; checking the dimensions of materials to be used and numbering the material lists; calculating weights, volumes and stress factors and their effect on the technical aspects of the design; locating and identifying symbols representing geological and geophysical formations or oilfield facilities in topographic surveys; tracing or copying drawings with tracing paper or cloth, ink and pencil; preparing coloured drawings of landscape and interior designs for clients; calculating heat loss and heat gain of buildings and structures using standard procedures to determine the specifications of equipment needed; and using drone technology to obtain aerial views and terrain data for civil engineering projects. This page does not constitute an opinion on practice or qualification examinations.

Three editorial self-test tasks: complete five drawings from the fictional dimensions, levels and services data given in the path section; check the constraints set in the question and list the items to be confirmed regarding the application of regulations separately; and use the six-item specialist conflict table to write a briefing note of no more than 500 characters. The exercise is not evidence for real design, construction or recruitment.

People who are more likely to adapt: those willing to check drawings and technical documents in detail over the long term and revise them repeatedly (32% consider precision or accuracy extremely important and 62% very important; 27% consider the consequences of error very serious, 34% serious and 24% somewhat serious), those able to produce drawings steadily to a fixed schedule and accept multi-disciplinary cooperation (94% have a regular fixed schedule and 73% work 40 hours per week; 65% consider teamwork extremely important and 23% very important), those able to communicate externally and internally by email and telephone (85% use email every day, 58% have telephone conversations every day and 50% are in contact with others most of the time), and those able to stop, record and escalate when drawing conflicts or an insufficient basis are found, in line with drafting standards and the review process. Risk is usually greater if the person finds long hours drawing and revising at a computer hard to accept (99% are indoors in a controlled environment every day, 37% sit more than half the time and 59% use their hands to handle tools continuously or almost continuously), is unwilling to check item by item against drafting standards and review rules, or is uncomfortable with visiting sites to collect survey data and supporting construction.

US 17-3011: the May 2025 median wage is 66,150 US dollars; 104,100 jobs in 2025 and growth of 5% over 2025—2035, with about 9,100 openings a year. The group of drafters is 180,200 jobs with a median wage of 68,090 US dollars, growth of 1% and about 14,400 openings a year, and the scope is labelled separately. The Chinese NBS release does not list drafter wages separately; industry wages serve only as background and qualifications and sealing are checked against the actual professional regulations.

In one sentence: a technical post that turns the concepts, calculations, specifications and site data of architects and engineers into reviewable, briefable and buildable architectural and civil drawings and, under professional supervision, completes coordination, checking, revision and delivery.

The work of architectural and civil drafters can be divided into four categories: drafting and presentation (using CAD or hand tools to draw scale plans of foundations, buildings and structures from concepts, sketches and engineering calculations, deciding on presentations such as orthographic or isometric drawings, and completing and reproducing drawings and document sets); data and code checking (analysing the impact of building codes, local regulations and spatial and site requirements on the design, reviewing sketches, drawings, specifications and other engineering data for conformity with the design concept, and evaluating information to determine compliance with standards); specialist cooperation and site support (coordinating structural, electrical and mechanical designs and determining how floor plans are presented, explaining drawings to production or construction teams and adjusting them as needed, visiting construction sites to collect survey data, and verifying on site under supervision that construction matches the design); and schedules and document preparation (determining the quality, cost, strength and quantity of materials and completing material lists, calculating weights, volumes and stress factors, preparing cost estimates, contracts, tender documents and technical reports under supervision, and drawing terrain and strata profiles and processing survey and investigation data).

O*NET 17-3011.00 Architectural and Civil Drafters: prepare detailed drawings of architectural and structural features of buildings, or drawings and topographical relief maps for civil engineering projects such as highways, bridges and public works, applying knowledge of building materials, engineering practices and mathematics to complete drawings. The common job titles listed on the page include Architectural Designer, Architectural Drafter, Architectural Draftsman, CAD Designer, CAD Tech, CADD Drafter, Civil Drafter, Drafting Technician, Draftsman and Draftsperson. The interest code is RCA (Realistic, Conventional, Artistic); the page lists 27 tasks. This occupation requires medium preparation (Job Zone Three, SVP 6.0 to below 7.0), usually needing vocational school training or related on-the-job experience or an associate degree; among the respondent answers 42% consider a bachelor's degree necessary. Of these tasks, 15 are core, 11 are supplementary, and 1 further new task of collecting site terrain by drone aerial photography has no importance score; this does not mean that everyone operates a drone. The 42% is a response about the education needed for new hires, not the education distribution of all practitioners.

Boundaries come down to four things: who is responsible for the design content and technical scheme, who signs and seals the drawings and bears the practice responsibility, who reviews and delivers the drawings, and who is responsible for construction and site safety. Drafters complete drafting, coordination, checking and revision under the guidance and supervision of an architect or engineer and deliver reviewable drawings and documents; the technical decisions and sealing of the design are borne by architects or engineers with the corresponding qualification; construction organisation and site safety are the responsibility of the construction unit; and planning permission and construction drawing review are the responsibility of the competent authorities and the review bodies. Drawings are professional documents and do not replace approval or contracting responsibility; where the scope of practice and the legal effect of drawings are involved, the regulations and institutional rules apply.

Under guidance and supervision, turn design concepts, calculations, specifications and survey data into reviewable, briefable and buildable drawings and technical documents, and deliver drawing versions and calculation and checking records.

Answer drafting delivery questions with: whether the drawing schedule and the drafting standards, sheet sizes and scales used are stated; whether dimensions, levels and material legends are checked item by item; whether the specialist conditions are closed; whether modifications and versions are traceable; and whether the work has been reviewed and sealed by personnel with the corresponding qualification.

Do not count adjacent responsibilities (the design scheme and technical decisions of architects and engineers, the practice sealing and statutory responsibility of registered personnel, construction to the drawings and site safety by the construction unit, quality and programme monitoring by the supervision unit, bills of quantities and pricing by cost personnel, control surveying and deliverables by survey personnel, and interior space and furnishing by interior designers) as core tasks of this occupation.

The objects are the graphic and data representation of buildings, structural members and civil and site works; the basis is the concepts, sketches, calculations, specifications and survey data provided by architects and engineers, together with drafting standards such as GB/T 50001-2017, Unified Standard for Building Drawing, and related engineering construction standards, building codes and local regulations, and it is subject to the institution's drafting and collaboration rules and drawing archive management requirements.

Architectural and civil drafters draw architectural, structural or civil drawings from design and survey input and check specialist conditions, dimensions, levels, materials and versions. Editorial checkpoints: dimensions and levels can be traced back to the input, the drawings meet the drafting standard used, specialist conflicts have a confirmation record, related drawings are checked after modification, and the delivered version and the review status are consistent. Sealing authority is checked separately against the statutory rules.

Architectural and structural construction drawings and details, general layout and site, terrain and section drawings, specialist cooperation and condition records, code compliance checklists, material lists and quantities and calculation records, drawing indexes and layer and file naming notes, modification notices and version and review records, and briefing and site cooperation and technical investigation reports.

Before starting, check the unit's business qualification and project type, one's own drafting and checking role, the person responsible for registered sealing, the version modification and delivery process, site arrangements, and data authorisation and confidentiality requirements. Internal institutional authorisation cannot replace statutory registration qualification.

Responsibility is divided according to the actual division of work: drafting personnel check the drawings and the input; professional designers confirm the scheme, calculations and specialist conditions; the unit is responsible for design quality; and statutory registered sealing follows the professional rules. Construction, supervision, surveying, costing and review each have their own responsibilities and cannot be summarised and replaced by a single drafting post.

Drafting work must follow the standards and confidentiality requirements: drawings should be produced to the drafting standards and the institution's collaboration and layer rules, drawings, calculations and review records must not be forged or tampered with, the name of a registered architect or registered engineer must not be used to sign or seal, and the work of others or unauthorised material must not be used without permission; drawings, technical data and client information should be handled in line with confidentiality and personal information protection requirements, and image libraries and standard drawing sets involving third-party copyright should be used within the authorised scope.

When the concepts, sketches or calculation data are incomplete or mutually contradictory, the code version on which the drawings are based is unclear, the specialist conditions are not closed, survey data is missing or does not match the site, or modification notices and versions cannot be traced, the relevant drafting work should be paused, the architect or engineer consulted and the data corrected, handled through the institution's review and modification process, and drawings that have not been reviewed or lack an adequate basis must not be issued because of schedule pressure.

Drawings apply only to a specific project, design stage, code version and drafting standard; the same building may be drawn and built differently under a different scheme or different professional conditions, construction and permit application should be based on the latest version that has been reviewed and sealed, process-stage drawings, scheme-stage drawings or unreviewed drawings must not be treated as a basis for construction, and layers and files from different versions must not be mixed.

Before starting, check at least six items: work direction (architectural drafting, civil and site drafting, structural and building services cooperation, construction drawing development and as-built documentation, and so on); drawing and review authority (whether the work is done independently or to the instructions of an architect or engineer, who reviews and seals, and how drawing versions and the modification process are managed); working method and intensity (long hours of computer drafting and repeated multi-disciplinary revision, the working week and schedule (94% regular fixed schedule, 73% 40 hours per week) and site visits and construction support arrangements); records and compliance requirements (sheet size, scale, layers and file naming, checking of dimensions and materials, confidentiality of client and project data, and authorised use of standards and drawing sets); employment and income method (full-time in a design or engineering unit, a technical department in a construction or manufacturing enterprise, consulting and drafting outsourcing, project-based or monthly, and whether project bonuses are included); and development path (deepening a specialist direction, moving into a professional designer or technical lead post, taking on sealing responsibility after obtaining registration, or moving into BIM and collaboration management or construction technology and costing).
Look at the work direction and the discipline drawn, not the job title.

Work directions: architectural drafting (plans, elevations, sections and details), civil and site drafting (general layout, terrain, sections and services), structural and building services cooperation, construction drawing development and materials and schedules, as-built drawings and operation and maintenance documentation, and BIM modelling and collaboration management; different directions differ in drawing types, counterpart disciplines, code emphasis and output form.

Mainland China: units take on survey and design work within their qualification scope; an unregistered person must not use the name of a registered practitioner. Drafter, designer and checker title blocks are filled in according to the person's actual role, and statutory registered signing and sealing follow the corresponding professional rules; support drafting does not equal obtaining registration authority.

Qualification and authority: check the actual education and software requirements, one's own drafting and checking role, and who bears the registered signing and sealing, and do not impersonate; professional design and sealing qualification must be met separately under the corresponding rules.
The working method, intensity and traceability requirements directly affect whether the work can be done compliantly and sustainably.

Working and compliance conditions: long hours drafting at a computer and eye, neck and shoulder strain, repeated multi-disciplinary revision and version turnover, a 94% regular fixed schedule and 73% working 40 hours per week, and travel and safety arrangements for site survey and construction support; sheet size, scale, layer and file naming standards, item-by-item checking of dimensions, materials and methods, modification notices and version and review traceability, confidentiality requirements for drawings, clients and project data, and archive retention and delivery rules for drawings and technical documents.
The nature of the institution and the project cycle affect long-term sustainability.

Employment and income method: stability and protection differ between full-time work in a design or engineering unit, a technical department in a construction or manufacturing enterprise, and consulting or drafting outsourcing; 73% work 40 hours per week and 94% have a regular fixed schedule, and income is affected by project sources, construction and manufacturing investment and the outsourcing pricing method, so it must be checked against the actual contract and project arrangements.
Drafting standards, professional software skills and the discipline drawn determine long-term development.

Development path: whether stable specialist capability can be built in one direction (architectural drafting, civil and site drafting, structural and building services cooperation, construction drawing development), whether CAD, BIM and professional calculation and data processing tools can be mastered, whether the person can move into a professional designer or technical lead post, obtain the corresponding registration after meeting the education and practice conditions and take on sealing responsibility, or move into BIM and collaboration management, construction technology and costing, or as-built and operation and maintenance documentation management.
Check the official and institutional requirements first, then decide on the investment.

Take the public information of the housing and urban-rural development authorities, the education authorities and employers as authoritative, and check whether the training direction and practical training conditions of the course applied for are compliant; do not readily trust non-official institutions' promises of guaranteed job recommendations or guaranteed certification, and do not take part in any arrangement involving sitting an examination for someone else, forging a drawing title block or signing drawings on someone's behalf.

Train drafting standards and software skills to a reviewable level: practise sheet sizes, scales, layers and dimension annotation against standards such as the Unified Standard for Building Drawing, master CAD and BIM modelling, drawing production and version management, and use a fictional project to complete a set of reviewable construction drawings and a material list, rather than producing presentation renderings only.
Practising drafters and detail designers

Give the automatable parts (repetitive annotation, drawing comparison, initial quantity and schedule estimating) to tools, shift effort to checking the drawing basis, specialist cooperation and conflict resolution, and the judgement of node and method representation, and keep review and modification records for every issued drawing.
Design institutions and engineering and construction enterprises

Editorial suggestion: establish layer, naming, version and permission rules and let the unit arrange drafting and checking according to the division of posts; the statutory registered name and sealing follow the applicable professional rules, and not all checking personnel should be recorded as registered personnel. Verify the tool steps first, and manage drawings and client data under institutional authorisation.
Education and vocational training institutions

Shift the focus of courses from pure software operation to standards, detailing, specialist cooperation and drawing checking, arrange practical training based on real drafting standards and fictional projects, and make clear that tool skills do not equal design judgement and practice responsibility.

The key to fit is observable behaviour: whether drawings can be produced steadily to the drafting standards and the layer and naming rules, whether dimensions, levels, materials and the codes on which they are based can be checked item by item, whether records and explanations are given truthfully under specialist conflict and rework pressure, and whether drawing at a computer and repeated revision can be accepted over the long term (99% are indoors in a controlled environment every day, 37% sit more than half the time, 32% consider precision or accuracy extremely important and 27% consider the consequences of error very serious). paragraphs: The risk scenarios on this page are an editorial summary; technical requirements are governed by the applicable engineering standards and institutional processes and registration authority by the regulations, and no accident rate or uniform penalty conclusion is provided. Mainland China: units take on survey and design work within their qualification scope; an unregistered person must not use the name of a registered practitioner. Drafter, designer and checker title blocks are filled in according to the person's actual role, and statutory registered signing and sealing follow the corresponding professional rules; support drafting does not equal obtaining registration authority.

There are four main categories of risk: drawings and data (errors in entering dimensions, levels, materials and schedules, missing items and specialist conflicts on drawings, and versions and layers out of control); authority and responsibility (issuing drawings without review, using another person's name to seal, and unclear responsibility for specialist cooperation and modification); site and personal (traffic and work safety when visiting sites to collect survey data and supporting construction, and the health load of long hours of computer work); and information and compliance (leakage of client and project data, the authorised use of image libraries, standards and third-party material, and incomplete archiving).

O*NET provides work context on precision, consequences of error, sitting, communication and site work, which is used to identify risk steps; the Chinese Regulations provide unit qualification, the registered name and the boundary of design modification. The scenarios and handling suggestions below are compiled editorially and are not accident statistics.
All drafting and development posts

If wrong dimensions, levels or material quantities go undetected and are used for construction or procurement, they may cause rework, cost or safety problems; responsibility is judged from the actual conduct, the contract and the applicable rules, and the bearer is not determined automatically by the error itself.

Apply double checking or sample re-checking to key dimensions, levels, materials and schedule data, re-check the affected locations after modification, and keep the checking records and versions in line with the institutional process.

The concepts, sketches or calculation data behind the drawings are incomplete or mutually contradictory, the drafting standard version is unclear, modification notices are not implemented on the drawings, or the checking step is skipped when the drawing deadline is tight.
All delivery and drawing issue posts

If drawings with an insufficient basis or checking are used as formal submission or construction documents, the basis and the responsibility may become unclear; ordinary working draft circulation, formal delivery and statutory registered sealing are checked separately.

Check and mark the confirmation status according to the unit's division of work; the registered name and sealing follow the professional rules, and not all checking roles should be recorded as registered personnel. The Regulations provide that construction drawings may only be used for construction after the stipulated review and approval; the rules applicable to a specific project are checked separately, and internal or controlled circulation of an ordinary draft does not equal construction use.
Issuing drawings first on grounds of schedule pressure, mixing drawing versions and approval status during circulation, and conveying checking comments only verbally without writing them back.
Posts involving client, project, tender and cost data, and posts using external material and image libraries

Leakage of client and project data and drawings may cause breach of contract and loss of trust; using unauthorised image libraries, standards or third-party material may lead to infringement disputes.

Handle drawings and data in line with the institution's confidentiality and information management requirements, use approved platforms and image libraries and standards within the authorised scope, and confirm the authorisation and redaction scope before providing anything externally.
Uploading drawings or project data to unauthorised tools, sending them to unrelated people, or publishing screenshots of drawings containing project information on public channels.
Posts that visit sites to collect survey data and support construction, and posts with long hours of computer work

O*NET supports visiting sites to survey where necessary and the context of indoor work, sitting and hand use, and does not provide injury or illness rates. The editorial risk-identification suggestion is: check the actual conditions of site travel, work and continuous computer operation; vision, neck, shoulder or wrist disorders must not be diagnosed from these occupational descriptions.

Wear protective equipment to site safety requirements and implement travel and insurance arrangements, follow the constructor's safety management when entering a construction site; arrange continuous eye use, posture and rest sensibly, and report anomalies as the institution requires.

Entering a site without following the site safety requirements or without protective equipment, continuing long-distance driving and travel in severe weather, and continuous long hours of eye use and sitting without arranging rest.
All drafting and collaboration posts

If multiple rounds of modification or several tool copies are not versioned consistently, the wrong version may be used for briefing or construction, with rework disputes; the rate of occurrence was not obtained on this page.
Unify layer, naming, version and permission rules, keep modification notices and version records, and confirm before delivery that the latest reviewed version is being used.
The same drawing number exists in several versions with non-standard naming, modifications are made on different copies, and the collaboration platform and local files coexist without being merged.
Posts involving specialist cooperation, briefing and modification

Delivering before specialist conditions or conflicts are confirmed may cause construction misreading and responsibility disputes; the consequences also depend on the checking and the user, and not every conflict necessarily becomes a construction error.

Register specialist conditions and conflicts item by item and make clear the proposed representation changes and the items to be confirmed, confirm the recipient and the version at briefing, and write back and notify the related disciplines after modification.

Conveying specialist conditions verbally without writing them back onto the drawings, not confirming the version and the responsible person at briefing, and not notifying the related disciplines after modification.

The Regulations support unit qualification, the registered name, the design basis and modification responsibility; the editorial suggestion is to confirm specialist conditions according to the real division of work, and not to equate keeping a record with authorisation to modify.

items.title: What do employers usually look at during recruitment?

values: Fictional question and input

Exercise input (all fictional, units in m): Yunpu Road community reading room, a single-storey rectangular building with an outer boundary of 12 × 8; the south-west corner is the building's local origin (0,0) and north is +y. Grid lines 1/2/3 are at x = 0/6/12 and A/B/C at y = 0/4/8; in this question the grid lines also serve as the locating lines for the outer wall boundary, and the 0.20 wall thickness is drawn inwards, and they are not a real structural grid. Indoors there is one open room with no internal walls; the floor is ±0.000 = absolute 100.20, the flat roof top is +3.600 = 103.80, the roof is shown with a thickness of 0.20 drawn downwards and there is no parapet. The south door is centred at x = 6 with an opening 1.20 wide and 2.10 high; the windows in the south wall are centred at x = 3/9, each 1.50 wide and 1.20 high with a sill at +0.90; the other three sides have no doors or windows. From this the plan, the south elevation and the section looking east along x = 6 can be drawn directly.

Site input (absolute coordinates in m): a 40 × 30 rectangular plot with its south-west corner at (0,0), and the building's local origin located at site (10,10). A road runs along the southern boundary y = 0; the existing ground is 100.00 at x = 0 and 100.60 at x = 40, rising linearly along x while y stays the same. An existing pipe runs along y = 14 from x = 0 to 40, with an outer diameter of 0.40 and a centre absolute elevation of 99.70; draw the east-west section along y = 14 and mark the building projection x = 10—22 and the pipe. The height limit set in the question is that the roof must not exceed 4.00 above the indoor floor, and this scheme at 3.60 satisfies only this question's setting and cannot be used to judge regulatory compliance.

Six specialist conditions requiring confirmation: S1 structural gives a door opening centred at x = 5.5, conflicting with the architectural x = 6; S2 structural roof top at +3.50 conflicts with the architectural +3.60. P1 plumbing proposes a connection pipe along y = 12 while the existing pipe is at y = 14; P2 the proposed connection centre at 99.90 differs from the existing 99.70. E1 the electrical box is drawn inside the south door opening at x = 5.4—6.6; E2 the proposed cable route at y = 14 shares the corridor with the existing pipe and has no burial depth. Record the discipline, the conflict, the proposed handling, the responsible role and the confirmation status separately, and do not determine structural or building services parameters yourself.

Material and change input: M1 floor indicative finish measured at an internal clear length of 11.60 × width of 7.60, thickness 0.02; M2 roof indicative protective layer measured at 12 × 8, thickness 0.03; M3 1 south door and M4 2 south windows, with opening sizes as above. Only the geometric net quantity is calculated, without allowance for waste and without counting structure or cost. A fictional client letter asks for the to-be-verified accessibility item to be deleted and the roof layer to be thinned: keep the to-be-verified item, do not carry out the thinning for now, register the request and pass it to the responsible designer for confirmation; there is no complete input on accessibility, fire protection, structure or material performance, so a compliance conclusion cannot be issued.
Drawing delivery

A3 landscape sheet size (editorial convention for this question) for five drawings: plan, south elevation and section at x=6 at 1:100; site general layout at 1:200; and the cross-section at y=14 at 1:200 both horizontally and vertically. Each drawing states the drawing number, orientation, scale, version V0, units and the fictional exercise purpose; grid lines, dimensions, levels, doors and windows and services are checked item by item.

Also submit the net material quantity schedule, the six-item conflict table and a briefing of no more than 500 characters; the code checking table is divided into checked against the question and to be checked with specialists and regulations, without inventing clauses or registered sealing.
Reference answers and checking order

The plan outer boundary is 12 × 8, which at 1:100 is 120 × 80 mm on the sheet; the internal clear wall dimensions are 11.60 × 7.60, an area of 88.16 sq m. The south door opening is x = 5.40—6.60, and the two window openings are x = 2.25—3.75 and 8.25—9.75. On the elevation the window sill is +0.90 and the head +2.10, the door head is +2.10 and the roof top is +3.60. In the section at x = 6 the internal clear height to the indicative roof underside is 3.40; the absolute ground is 100.20 and the roof 103.80.

In the general layout the four building corners are (10,10)/(22,10)/(22,18)/(10,18), and the plot is 200 × 150 mm on the sheet. In the section the existing ground is 100.15 at x = 10 and 100.33 at x = 22; the pipe top is 99.90 and the pipe bottom 99.50, and the pipe overlaps the building projection, so the responsible personnel must decide on protection or diversion and must not issue a foundation scheme on their own. Materials: M1 net area 88.16 sq m and volume 1.7632 m³; M2 area 96 sq m and volume 2.88 m³; M3 1 door and M4 2 windows.

All six conflicts remain to be confirmed: S1 re-check the door position, S2 confirm the roof level, P1 confirm the connection route, P2 confirm the connection level, E1 moving it out of the door opening requires specialist confirmation, and E2 add the cable level and clearance conditions. The responsible roles are structural, plumbing and electrical respectively, and the architectural personnel consolidate. Until the input is confirmed, the suggestions must not be treated as final design in version V1 within the drawing set.

This question does not constitute a real design, construction, qualification or recruitment test. Record according to your own actual role and do not use registered sealing; use only your own geometry and authorised material.

entries.answer: Every day is mainly spent drawing scale drawings and details with computer-aided drafting systems or plotters and hand tools, expressing the design intent from concepts, sketches, calculations and specification sheets, analysing the impact of building codes, local regulations and site requirements on the design, coordinating structural, electrical and mechanical designs and determining how floor plans are presented, completing material lists and checking dimensions and materials, and where necessary visiting sites to collect survey data or explaining drawings to construction and production teams; the work is mainly indoor computer work (99% are indoors in a controlled environment every day), with 94% on a regular fixed schedule and 73% working 40 hours per week.
entries.question: What does an architectural and civil drafter do every day?

entries.answer: Drafters turn design input into reviewable drawings and complete checking and delivery under the guidance and supervision of an architect or engineer; architects and engineers bear the design scheme and technical decisions and sign and seal design documents, a different responsibility and qualification system; construction managers are responsible for construction organisation and on-site programme, quality and safety; mechanical drafters and electrical and electronics drafters use different standard systems and drawing types; building and construction inspectors carry out inspection and determination to regulations and acceptance requirements; and cost estimators are responsible for quantity calculation and pricing. When choosing a direction, the output, responsibility and qualification requirements should each be checked.

entries.answer: Look at three observable behaviours: whether drawings can be produced steadily to the drafting standards and the layer and naming rules and dimensions, levels and materials checked item by item; whether records and explanations are given truthfully under specialist conflict and rework pressure; and whether drawing at a computer and repeated revision can be accepted over the long term (32% consider precision or accuracy extremely important and 62% very important; 27% consider the consequences of error very serious). The O*NET interest code is RCA (Realistic, Conventional, Artistic) and serves only as a starting reference, not as a basis for recruitment or a skills test.
